content.value:
After backs spasms kept sidelined for the past two games, wide receiver Ladd McConkey returned to practice on Wednesday but participated in a limited fashion. He was one of five players who logged limited practices, joining cornerback Donte Jackson (groin), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (knee), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf).

The six remaining players on the injury report were all DNPs. Edge rusher Khalil Mack received his usual veteran’s rest day to begin the new week, but the other five players who worked off to the side were cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring), cornerback Rodney Shelley (ankle), tight end Charlie Kolar (concussion), and linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee).

Henley played 61 of 69 snaps against the Ravens on Monday night and Jim Harbaugh told reporters earlier Wednesday he would sit out practice with knee soreness.

Pipkins’ return could be something to watch should he be activated off of injured reserve this week. Harbaugh told reporters that rookie Logan Taylor would remain the starter after a standout performance against the Ravens. If right guard Cole Strange continues to underperform, there may be a chance Pipkins could relieve him of his duties. Kayode Awosika, who is now healthy, would also be a name to watch for that scenario, as well.

content.value:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Chargers fans and fans across the country.

After the Chargers beat the Ravens on Monday Night Football for their first win of the season, they fell out of the No. 1 spot to No. 2 behind the 1-8 Tennessee Titans. With the Jets up next, and a host of other teams without their starting quarterbacks, the Chargers could very well win their way out of a shot at picking first overall.

In this week’s Reacts poll, I want to know how you’re all feeling about potentially dropping out of the top three picks and missing out on a true franchise-changing prospect.

Go ahead and hop into the poll below to let us know how you feel!

Are you ok with the Chargers missing the No. 1 pick?

Are you confident in the Chargers?

content.value:
The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop.

Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton’s 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and a rushing score, as well.

Speaking of ground games, the Chargers held the Ravens to almost nothing on the ground. All-Pro back Derrick Henry was limited to just 10 yards on 10 carries. The zero yards on the ground for Baltimore during the first half was a historic low for the franchise.

You can’t be much more dominant than that.

Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Monday night.

Offense

Best

TE Charlie Kolar – 74.8
OG Logan Taylor – 74.4
QB Justin Herbert – 73.0
WR Tre’ Harris – 72.0
FB Scott Matlock – 70.2

It was poetic for Kolar — the former Baltimore Raven — to catch the first-down pass that helped seal the win over his former team. He was also dyamite in the run game, posting the second-high run block grade with a 74.6. His 76.4 pass block grade was also fourth best on the night.

Monday was Taylor’s best performance as a pro, finishing with zero pressures or sacks allowed on 27 dropbacks. His 81.1 pass block grade was tops on the team while his 68.9 in run blocking was fourth best.

For the first time all season, Herbert did not throw an interception and it led to his highest game grade of 2026.

Harris caught five passes for 86 yards all in the first half. Unfortunately he caught zero passes in the final 30 minutes of game time, but his yardage still gave him a new season and career high.

During the broadcast, it was shown that, at one point, the Chargers were averaging 5.1 yards per carry with Matlock on the field and 3.8 when he was not. He’s done an excellent job as the team’s starting fullback and I believe the switch from a zone-heavy run scheme to a gap scheme has benefitted both him and Hampton.

Worst

OT Travis Burke – 39.5
WR Quentin Johnston – 52.4
OG Cole Strange – 53.4
WR Derius Davis – 53.6
WR Theo Wease Jr. – 54.1

Unfortunately the team’s first win of the year was also one of Burke’s worst performances of the season. He allowed a team-high five pressures and had an abysmal 27.9 pass block grade to go with a penalty. The next worse grade among the offensive line was Strange with an above-average 64.0.

Johnston finished with one catch on one target for six yards. His season may be one of the biggest failures for Mike McDaniel in a season packed to the brim with them.

The aforementioned Strange allowed four pressures and was also called for a penalty. His 57.3 in run block was below average but still better than Joe Alt’s 53.2.

Defense

Best

LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 90.6
DT Teair Tart – 82.8
CB Donte Jackson – 77.4
EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 73.7
EDGE Khalil Mack – 73.0

What a night for Phillips, and also what a season it’s turning into for the first-year NFL starter. Phillips was a menace against the run on Monday night, helping the Chargers hold Derrick Henry to just 10 yards on 10 carries. He also snagged the team’s only interception off Jacoby Brissett when he sprinted under a deflected by Cam Hart. All night long, his high effort was apparent.

Tart had his highest-graded game of the season overall to go with his season-high 81.7 pass rush grade. He tied a season-high of three pressures, as well.

Jackson rebounded after a rough performance against the Texans to allow just one catch for six yards in three targets his way.

Mack and Tuli combined for 15 pressures on Brissett with the latter recording a nine by himself. His previous season high was six in Week Three.

Worst

S R.J. Mickens – 25.1
CB Deane Leonard – 28.5
S Elijah Molden – 40.9
LB Daiyan Henley – 51.7
DT Jamaree Caldwell – 53.9

Mickens luckily knocked down the Hail Mary attempt by the Ravens to seal the team’s first win of the season, but it was otherwise a bad night for the second-year safety. His overall game grade was his worst of the year by far and his 26.6 coverage grade was very much the same. Mickens was also called for his third penalty of the season.

Molden was credited with allowing five receptions on six targets towards him for 65 yards, including 53 after the catch. Henley also was dinged a bunch in coverage. PFF has him credited with a whopping nine receptions allowed on 11 targets in his area.

content.value:
The Chargers finally got their first win of the season by beating the Ravens on Monday Night Football who were forced to start quarterback Jacoby Brissett due to both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley being hurt. In Week 11, the Bolts could once again face a team without their starting quarterback if Geno Smith, who did not finish their most recent loss to the Bills, remains sidelined.

If that is the case, it would be backup Cade Klubnik manning the offense. Klubnik’s first ever NFL action came in Week 10, meaning the Chargers would have a much higher chance of winning their second consecutive game should he earn the start.

If Smith does end up pushing through and starting, then I’d start viewing this matchup as a toss-up. Smith has 12 touchdowns to just three picks this year as he’s gotten back to playing fairly good ball in his first season back with the Jets.

Defensively, the Jets are middle-of-the-pack. They rank 16th in total defense (332.1) and 22nd in scoring defense (25.4). The Chargers offense was better — at least on the ground — against the Ravens but the passing attacked remained underwhelming. Justin Herbert threw for just 38 yards on three completions in all of the final 30 minutes with only three players seeing more than two receptions, and only one of them was a wide receiver (Tre’ Harris).

With the Jets ranking fifth in pass defense this season, the Chargers’ game plan may end up being much of the same this week.

content.value:
Just like we all could have predicted, the Chargers’ Sunday Night Football matchup against the Patriots has been flexed out of primetime by the NFL and replaced by Raiders-Browns. The Chargers and Patriots will now play at 1:05 p.m.

The news was expected after Patriots starting quarterback Drake Maye went down with an ankle injury against the Lions in Germany that looks to be season-ending. Behind Maye, the Patriots have Tommy DeVito as their backup. Turns out, the NFL does not think it would be a good idea to keep the 1-8 Chargers and the DeVito-led Pats in one of the week’s three primetime slots.

After this flex, the Chargers only have one other primetime game remaining on the schedule and that comes on December 16th for Thursday Night Football. There’s only been one other Thursday Night Football game that’s ever been flexed, so it’s likely the Chargers get to keep this one against a very good opponent.

After backs spasms kept sidelined for the past two games, wide receiver Ladd McConkey returned to practice on Wednesday but participated in a limited fashion. He was one of five players who logged limited practices, joining cornerback Donte Jackson (groin), defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe (ankle), offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (knee), and safety Kendall Williamson (calf).

The six remaining players on the injury report were all DNPs. Edge rusher Khalil Mack received his usual veteran’s rest day to begin the new week, but the other five players who worked off to the side were cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring), cornerback Rodney Shelley (ankle), tight end Charlie Kolar (concussion), and linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee).

Henley played 61 of 69 snaps against the Ravens on Monday night and Jim Harbaugh told reporters earlier Wednesday he would sit out practice with knee soreness.

Pipkins’ return could be something to watch should he be activated off of injured reserve this week. Harbaugh told reporters that rookie Logan Taylor would remain the starter after a standout performance against the Ravens. If right guard Cole Strange continues to underperform, there may be a chance Pipkins could relieve him of his duties. Kayode Awosika, who is now healthy, would also be a name to watch for that scenario, as well.

content.value:
The Chargers beat the Ravens to move to 1-8 on the season. The 0-17 jokes and hypotheticals can all finally stop.

Justin Herbert and the offense took a step forward with zero turnovers and a dominating performance on the ground with 160 yards, spurred by Omarion Hampton’s 105-yard night. Herbert also added 51 yards and a rushing score, as well.

Speaking of ground games, the Chargers held the Ravens to almost nothing on the ground. All-Pro back Derrick Henry was limited to just 10 yards on 10 carries. The zero yards on the ground for Baltimore during the first half was a historic low for the franchise.

You can’t be much more dominant than that.

Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Monday night.

Offense

Best

TE Charlie Kolar – 74.8
OG Logan Taylor – 74.4
QB Justin Herbert – 73.0
WR Tre’ Harris – 72.0
FB Scott Matlock – 70.2

It was poetic for Kolar — the former Baltimore Raven — to catch the first-down pass that helped seal the win over his former team. He was also dyamite in the run game, posting the second-high run block grade with a 74.6. His 76.4 pass block grade was also fourth best on the night.

Monday was Taylor’s best performance as a pro, finishing with zero pressures or sacks allowed on 27 dropbacks. His 81.1 pass block grade was tops on the team while his 68.9 in run blocking was fourth best.

For the first time all season, Herbert did not throw an interception and it led to his highest game grade of 2026.

Harris caught five passes for 86 yards all in the first half. Unfortunately he caught zero passes in the final 30 minutes of game time, but his yardage still gave him a new season and career high.

During the broadcast, it was shown that, at one point, the Chargers were averaging 5.1 yards per carry with Matlock on the field and 3.8 when he was not. He’s done an excellent job as the team’s starting fullback and I believe the switch from a zone-heavy run scheme to a gap scheme has benefitted both him and Hampton.

Worst

OT Travis Burke – 39.5
WR Quentin Johnston – 52.4
OG Cole Strange – 53.4
WR Derius Davis – 53.6
WR Theo Wease Jr. – 54.1

Unfortunately the team’s first win of the year was also one of Burke’s worst performances of the season. He allowed a team-high five pressures and had an abysmal 27.9 pass block grade to go with a penalty. The next worse grade among the offensive line was Strange with an above-average 64.0.

Johnston finished with one catch on one target for six yards. His season may be one of the biggest failures for Mike McDaniel in a season packed to the brim with them.

The aforementioned Strange allowed four pressures and was also called for a penalty. His 57.3 in run block was below average but still better than Joe Alt’s 53.2.

Defense

Best

LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 90.6
DT Teair Tart – 82.8
CB Donte Jackson – 77.4
EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 73.7
EDGE Khalil Mack – 73.0

What a night for Phillips, and also what a season it’s turning into for the first-year NFL starter. Phillips was a menace against the run on Monday night, helping the Chargers hold Derrick Henry to just 10 yards on 10 carries. He also snagged the team’s only interception off Jacoby Brissett when he sprinted under a deflected by Cam Hart. All night long, his high effort was apparent.

Tart had his highest-graded game of the season overall to go with his season-high 81.7 pass rush grade. He tied a season-high of three pressures, as well.

Jackson rebounded after a rough performance against the Texans to allow just one catch for six yards in three targets his way.

Mack and Tuli combined for 15 pressures on Brissett with the latter recording a nine by himself. His previous season high was six in Week Three.

Worst

S R.J. Mickens – 25.1
CB Deane Leonard – 28.5
S Elijah Molden – 40.9
LB Daiyan Henley – 51.7
DT Jamaree Caldwell – 53.9

Mickens luckily knocked down the Hail Mary attempt by the Ravens to seal the team’s first win of the season, but it was otherwise a bad night for the second-year safety. His overall game grade was his worst of the year by far and his 26.6 coverage grade was very much the same. Mickens was also called for his third penalty of the season.

Molden was credited with allowing five receptions on six targets towards him for 65 yards, including 53 after the catch. Henley also was dinged a bunch in coverage. PFF has him credited with a whopping nine receptions allowed on 11 targets in his area.

content.value:
The Chargers finally got their first win of the season by beating the Ravens on Monday Night Football who were forced to start quarterback Jacoby Brissett due to both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley being hurt. In Week 11, the Bolts could once again face a team without their starting quarterback if Geno Smith, who did not finish their most recent loss to the Bills, remains sidelined.

If that is the case, it would be backup Cade Klubnik manning the offense. Klubnik’s first ever NFL action came in Week 10, meaning the Chargers would have a much higher chance of winning their second consecutive game should he earn the start.

If Smith does end up pushing through and starting, then I’d start viewing this matchup as a toss-up. Smith has 12 touchdowns to just three picks this year as he’s gotten back to playing fairly good ball in his first season back with the Jets.

Defensively, the Jets are middle-of-the-pack. They rank 16th in total defense (332.1) and 22nd in scoring defense (25.4). The Chargers offense was better — at least on the ground — against the Ravens but the passing attacked remained underwhelming. Justin Herbert threw for just 38 yards on three completions in all of the final 30 minutes with only three players seeing more than two receptions, and only one of them was a wide receiver (Tre’ Harris).

With the Jets ranking fifth in pass defense this season, the Chargers’ game plan may end up being much of the same this week.

content.value:
Just like we all could have predicted, the Chargers’ Sunday Night Football matchup against the Patriots has been flexed out of primetime by the NFL and replaced by Raiders-Browns. The Chargers and Patriots will now play at 1:05 p.m.

The news was expected after Patriots starting quarterback Drake Maye went down with an ankle injury against the Lions in Germany that looks to be season-ending. Behind Maye, the Patriots have Tommy DeVito as their backup. Turns out, the NFL does not think it would be a good idea to keep the 1-8 Chargers and the DeVito-led Pats in one of the week’s three primetime slots.

After this flex, the Chargers only have one other primetime game remaining on the schedule and that comes on December 16th for Thursday Night Football. There’s only been one other Thursday Night Football game that’s ever been flexed, so it’s likely the Chargers get to keep this one against a very good opponent.

content.value:
The Chargers finally did it.

After 10 weeks and nine games into the 2026 season, Jim Harbaugh and the Bolts finally got their first win of the season by beating the Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football. It was the team’s most complete game of the season, which included zero turnovers from Justin Herbert and over 160 yards rushing.

The win put the Chargers tied with the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins at 1-8. For the most parts, experts put either one of these teams at the very bottom, but the good news is that it is no longer a clean sweep by the Chargers!

That’s something worth celebrating, right?

…right?

Anyhoo, here’s where the Chargers landed in this week’s power rankings after their first win!

Pro Football Talk – #29

“John Harbaugh says hello.” – Mike Florio

ESPN – #31

“Non-QB MVP at midseason: Edge Tuli Tuipulotu”

“It’s hard to find value in the Chargers’ one-win debacle, but the defense has at least been passable. And there’s no doubt that Tuipulotu is the best player on that unit. The 2023 second-round pick has a team-high 22 pressures and is tied for the team lead with three sacks. His average run tackle comes after a gain of just 2.2 yards.” – Aaron Schatz

CBS Sports – #31

“They climbed out of the cellar by winning for the first time Monday night against the Ravens. Can you believe it?” – Pete Prisco

The Athletic – #31

“Breakout player: Tré Harris”

“The second-year wide receiver, a second-round pick out of Ole Miss, set a new career high in yards in a season Monday night after catching five passes for a career-high 86 yards. He now has 348 for the season. It took one sliding and reviewed catch to get there, but it helped the Chargers get their first win.” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff

Bleacher Report – #32

“The Los Angeles Chargers finally have their first win. And while that one victory isn’t enough to get them out of the basement of these Power Rankings, it’s a start at least.”

“After weeks of a backfield committee that was…let’s go with confusing, the Chargers handed the keys in the backfield back to 2025 first-round pick Omarion Hampton. In doing so the Bolts may have unlocked something—Hampton racked up 105 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries.”

“After a brutal stretch in the schedule, things let up some going forward—not one of the Chargers’ next four opponents has a winning record.”

“The 2026 season is lost—and has been for a while. But there’s an opportunity for the Chargers to build some momentum over the next month, even if all it nets them is a lower pick in next year’s draft. – Brad Davenport

Yahoo Sports – #32

‘‘The Chargers got the win they needed to avoid a lot of annoying 0-17 questions. Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves; it was just one win, and on the whole, they’ve still been the NFL’s worst team this season. But give the Chargers credit for a good effort. They figured out how to make the Ravens one-dimensional. Baltimore had 16 yards rushing on 15 carries. That forced Baltimore to lean too much on quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was making his first Ravens start after being traded less than two weeks ago.”

‘‘It was also encouraging to see Omarion Hampton emerge with a 105-yard rushing day. Justin Herbert completed only 12 passes but he didn’t need to do much more because the running game was effective. Maybe the Chargers can build on their first win and have a respectable second half of the season.” – Frank Schwab

content.value:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-8 after beating the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 10. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the New York Jets at home in Week 11.

The Jets are fresh off a loss against the Buffalo Bills at home, where Gino Smith exited the game and was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik. Smith hurt his ankle against the Bills, which puts his status for the game in jeopardy.

The Bolts entered this week as 2.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The over/under is currently set at 40.5 points.

The Chargers picked up their first win of the season in a 23-20 victory on the road against the Ravens. Justin Herbert got things started with a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter. Omarion Hampton also found the end zone in the second quarter.

While the Ravens attempted to tighten the gap late with a 1-yard touchdown run from Derrick Henry, they were unable to complete the comeback, which gave the Chargers their first win of the season.

The Chargers’ win ensures that no team will go winless this season and gives them something to cheer about after eight straight losses. While Los Angeles might not be competing for a playoff spot, they can tag on some wins to give themselves something to build upon.

BFTB community, how do you feel about the Chargers starting a winning streak in Week 11 against the Jets? Let us know in the comments section below.

content.value:
The Chargers have given away the first overall pick after winning their first game of the season on Monday night. However, as current owners of the second overall pick, they’re still in a position to come out with amazing value on day one.

In a new 2027 mock draft by ESPN’s Jordan Reid, the Chargers end up trading out of the second slot with the Jets, which allows them to pick up an additional first-rounder.

With the first of their two picks (No. 4), the Bolts still land a top receiver in Indiana’s Charlie Becker. Here’s what Reid had to say about the pairing:

“The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their one-win start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact they already have a QB in Justin Herbert are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we’ll use this first pick to get Herbert some help.”

“Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert’s WR1.”

As for the 13th overall pick, Reid has the Chargers grabbing one of the best and most versatile offensive linemen in the class with Iowa’s Trevor Lauck, who can play both tackle and guard at the next level.

“After acquiring a pass catcher with their initial first-rounder, it’s time for the Chargers to give Justin Herbert some blocking help. Between the erratic health of tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt and the constant issues with the interior line, the Bolts have struggled to keep Herbert upright in the pocket. Lauck is a steady blocker who doesn’t have much flash but simply gets the job done, allowing just five pressures and zero sacks in 10 games this season. Scouts are mixed on where they see Lauck playing in the NFL, but that shouldn’t matter for a Los Angeles team that needs help across the entire line.”

What do you think of this potential draft haul for the Chargers? Yay or nay? Let us know your thoughts below!

content.value:
The Chargers began the season with Omarion Hampton as their lead back, but the second-year runner lost two fumbles in as many games to start the campaign and that quickly led the Bolts to a three-headed committee for the next month-plus.

In recent weeks, Hampton’s been garnering a larger share of the backfield touches, but Monday night’s performance was much more of what we all expected to be the norm week-in and week-out. Hampton carried the football more than 20 times and finished with 105 yards and a score, his first 100-yard game since Week 4 of last year. He looked strong, locked-in, and overall more comfortable as the game went on the more he touched the football.

This success on the ground or Hampton also coincided with a shift in the run game, going away from zone and more into gap and power schemes. Per James Koh of 97.1 The Fan in Los Angeles, the Chargers ran zone 53 percent of the time from Weeks One through Nine, but that number dropped to just 38 percent against the Ravens.

The shift away from zone for Hampton has been discussed at length this season, noting his success in gap schemes dating back to his time at North Carolina. On one of his best runs of the night, the Bolts pulled left tackle Joe Alt across the formation to kick out a defender in the hole and Hampton cut right off his backside for a gain of 19 to begin the second half.

Overall the Chargers ran for 164 yards on 34 carries, aided by Justin Herbert’s 51 yards off scrambles, to end the night averaging a strong 4.7 yards per tote.

Is this the new recipe moving forward for the Chargers? I wouldn’t be shocked in the slightest, if so.

content.value:
The Chargers enter their first primetime game of the season still winless and without much direction. When change was all but assured at the bye week, the Bolts somehow came out with zero moves made and kept on trucking like they weren’t at the bottom of the league in just about every offensive category.

They were also somehow worse than they were before the break.

Some much-needed offensive reinforcements are en route to return tonight, but will it be enough to move the needle in the right direction?

Under the lights, you just hope that it’s at least competitive and entertaining.

Enjoy the game, everyone! Bolt up!
